dedupe_keys.name: pipe incidents database search of ntsb and phmsa pipeline incident records gti

description: Pipe Incidents is a database search of natural gas and hazardous liquid pipeline incidents built by the Gas Technology Institute (GTI) from public records, in a research programme sponsored by US DOT PHMSA and Operations Technology Development. It combines incidents taken from NTSB pipeline accident investigation reports from 1969 to 2020 with PHMSA incident records for gas distribution (1984 to 2019), gas transmission and gathering (1984 to 2019) and hazardous liquid pipelines (1985 to 2019). The records were optimised for accuracy, consistency and redundancy, with formats normalised across the reporting periods, so that root causes can be analysed against pipeline properties, sites and operating characteristics. Coverage: US pipelines. Format and access: a web search application without registration. Licence and cost: free; no licence is stated, and GTI disclaims any warranty of accuracy or completeness. Caveats: the site says the search engine is not complete, needs periodic updates and ends in 2019 or 2020, and it is mainly for identifying recognised root causes. It supports hazard exposure and resilience studies of pipeline failure causes. It relates to the PHMSA incident data, NTSB CAROL investigations and the pipeline cyber-physical incident panel in the catalogue.
